subject: Urgent: MedSync streaming sessions dropping — proposed heartbeat + fallback playbook
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@medsync.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: ops+infra@medsync.com, customer-success@medsync.com
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming sessions dropping during high throughput window

Connor —

We started seeing a spike in 5xx/429s around 09:00 PT this morning and a bunch of our long-running interactive sessions are being cut short (clients report idle disconnects after ~18s). This is directly impacting active clinician workflows (they rely on streaming suggestions). We can reproduce by running concurrent scripted sessions (~120 concurrent live sessions) while pushing normal traffic.

Quick ask: can Redwood confirm whether this is a client-side timeout/keepalive issue or a server-side session eviction? We need a mitigation ASAP — even a temporary fallback to non-streaming completions would help.

Attached: a snippet of session logs and a capture of the failure window.

—Alex
Head of Platform, MedSync
From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@medsync.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:38:17 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming sessions dropping during high throughput window

Alex — thanks for the early heads-up and logs. 

Initial read: we see an increase in 429s coming from rate-limited routing plus simultaneous spike of 5xx errors on a subset of streaming nodes (nodes in us-west-2 pool B). We're triaging with infra now. Immediate mitigation options we can put in place in the next 30–60 minutes:

- Short-term: turn on automatic session keepalive probes from client SDK (heartbeat) to prevent idle disconnects while we stabilize routing. We can provide a small SDK patch and a recommended heartbeat payload (attached).
- Fallback: enable per-customer policy to route MedSync to non-streaming completions (batch-generated full responses) for requests tagged as interactive for up to 6 hours. This avoids stream semantics and reduces per-session resource pressure.
- Throttle: apply a soft throttle to bursty IPs and activate a conservative routing policy that favors nodes in pool A (lower CPU load).

Evelyn & Sean: can you confirm capacity on pool A and whether we can open the fallback route? Monica — please prepare an incident note and notify CS.

I'll provide a playbook in the next message with exact commands and rollback steps.

—Connor
Director, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:52:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming sessions dropping during high throughput window

On Sun, Aug 1, 2027 at 9:38 AM connor_obrien@redwood.com wrote:
> Evelyn & Sean: can you confirm capacity on pool A and whether we can open the fallback route?

We've looked at node telemetry for us-west-2. Pool A has ~20% spare GPU headroom if we re-route lower-priority tenants off it — we can accommodate MedSync for a short window. Pool B shows elevated kernel OOM traces and higher latencies on attention kernels under the 2k token path.

Actionable next steps from infra:
1) Sean to flip routing rule to favor pool A for MedSync (target traffic migration over 3 rolling steps).
2) Enable temporary non-streaming fallback route (config flag: medsync.force_full_completion=true) — this will cause SDK-tagged requests to use the non-stream generator endpoint.
3) Add a 10s TCP keepalive + application-level 15s heartbeat recommended payload to the client SDK. We'll attach the sample payload.

I'll coordinate with runtime to watch memory alloc graphs while we shift traffic.

—Evelyn
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, Alex Turner <alex.turner@medsync.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 10:25:11 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming sessions dropping during high throughput window

Alex / team — we've implemented the routing change and gradually moved MedSync traffic to pool A starting at 10:05 PT. Initial telemetry shows 429 rate dropping by ~60% for interactive endpoints and 5xx error rates for streaming nodes down by ~45%.

We also enabled the non-streaming fallback route at 10:15 PT for any request tagged with "interactive_v1" in the header. That change is reversible.

Note to Devs: please pull the SDK heartbeat patch from https://drive.redwood.com/teams/infra/medsync/heartbeat-sdk-v1 and add the payload below to sessions until we confirm stability. Sample heartbeat payload (application/json):
{
  "type": "heartbeat",
  "session_id": "<client-generated>",
  "ts": "<iso-ts>",
  "last_offset": 0
}

We'll keep monitoring and will revert to streaming once the kernel memory and queue latencies are stable.

—Sean
Lead SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@medsync.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 11:02:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming sessions dropping during high throughput window

Thanks — we rolled the SDK heartbeat to a subset of client hosts and have not seen further idle disconnects for those sessions. The fallback to full completions introduced a small latency increase (~120–200ms p95) but is acceptable as a temporary measure.

Couple of follow-ups we need:
- Can Redwood provide a short post-mortem with root cause and a timeline?
- We need to discuss whether longer-term fixes include: kernel-level attention memory safety patches, smarter batching that preserves streaming while avoiding KV-cache churn, or a dedicated pool for MedSync.

We also have a standing executive review on Wednesday and would like a 10-minute summary and the proposed remediation timeline.

—Alex
From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@medsync.com>, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 17:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming sessions dropping during high throughput window

Alex — quick update for your exec review:

Summary (for execs):
- Impact: brief surge of 5xx/429s caused a subset of long-lived streaming sessions to drop; approx 18–24 minutes of elevated failures during 09:00–09:30 PT window. No patient-safety incidents reported.
- Immediate mitigation: switched MedSync to pool A and enabled non-streaming fallback + client heartbeat. This stabilized customer experience within ~20 minutes.
- Short-term next steps (1–7 days):
  * Runtime team to implement kernel-level guardrails to reduce attention kernel memory pressure (INF-1129).
  * Product/SDK team to publish heartbeat and keepalive guidance and ship SDK patch (v2.4.1) that defaults to heartbeat for interactive sessions.
  * Ops to provision a dedicated micro-pool for MedSync as an option if they prefer isolation (costed estimate attached).
- Longer-term (1–3 months):
  * Improve batching/adaptive scheduling so streaming sessions don't compete with heavy batch workloads; consider a dynamic cache partitioning strategy.
  * Add a streaming health endpoint and SLA guardrail that triggers automatic fallback earlier to avoid client retry storms.

Open asks for MedSync before the Wednesday review: please confirm whether you want us to provision the dedicated micro-pool (we've attached a cost estimate), and let us know if the execs want a deeper dive on kernel fixes vs product mitigations.

We're preparing a concise 10-minute deck and will send it by EOD tomorrow.

—Connor
Director, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
